title: Quickfire Coverlet: Rolling Coverage Checklist (Feb 2028)
content:
Purpose:
One-page rolling checklist for quick ad-hoc coverage decisions and who-to-call during short service blips (throttles / regional capacity constraints / model fallback storms). Designed to be copied into a spreadsheet or used as a minute-by-minute log during handoffs.

How to use:
- Owner opens this doc and updates the "Status row" live.
- Timestamps in UTC.
- Keep entries terse (2–3 words) and tag with team shorthand (SRE, ENG, PROD, CS, SE).
- If an action is expected to take >30m, mark with "ESCALATE" and notify the on-call.

Quick summary (top-line):
- Trigger: unexpected 2x endpoint throttle in eu-west-1 on hosted-api (12:13–ongoing).
- Immediate mitigation tried: burst to dedicated fallback pool, reduced batch window to 40ms, temporary 0.5 quantization roll-back on small-models.
- Current risk: degraded 95th p99 latency for chat; potential cost spike if fallback persists.

Rolling checklist (copy rows into sheet):
- Timestamp | Action | Owner | Team | ETA | Status | Notes
- 2028-02-12T12:13Z | Detect throttle | Monitoring | SRE | 0m | done | rate-limiter fired, rule TL-EU-03
- 2028-02-12T12:14Z | Apply fallback routing | Diego Ramos | ENG | 2m | done | routed 30% traffic to eu-central fallback
- 2028-02-12T12:16Z | Reduce batch window | Maya Chen | serving-runtime | 5m | done | lowered to 40ms, tokens/sec up 8%
- 2028-02-12T12:20Z | Assess model quantization rollback | Tom Whitaker | optimize | 10m | in_progress | small models tested locally
- 2028-02-12T12:35Z | Customer comms draft | Nora Patel | CS | 15m | todo | short status for affected customers
- 2028-02-12T12:40Z | Cost watch toggle | Asha Menon | ops-coordination | 5m | todo | enable cost-alert thresholds for fallback pool
- 2028-02-12T12:50Z | Decide on regional failover | SRE lead | SRE | 20m | todo | if p95 > target continue failover

Coverage grid (who can act / fallback permissions):
- SRE: full throttle rules, regional failover permission, paging authority.
- ENG (serving-runtime): batch/kv-cache tweaks, kernel selection rollbacks (non-blocking).
- ENG (platform): capacity nudges to dedicated pool, schedule bursts.
- OPTIMIZE team: quantization and perf regressions, rollback/enable quick patches.
- CS/SE: external comms / customer triage / temporary SLAs.

Short one-off analysis (cost vs latency tradeoff snapshot):
- Baseline hosted p95 latency (eu-west-1): 220ms, token cost baseline: $0.0023/token.
- With 30% fallback to eu-central (different model variant): p95 latency rises to 310ms but unit cost drops 12% on routed units.
- If fallback persists >6h estimated extra monthly cost: +$12k (back-of-envelope).
- Quick decision rule suggested: accept latency up to +100ms for up to 2h if cost savings >5% and customer-impacted sessions <1.5% of daily active.

Open questions / triage notes:
- Why did TL-EU-03 trigger? False-positive on short burst or real capacity mismatch? Attach monitoring query (MON-queries-OPS-1147).
- Is quantization rollback safe for mid-sized models used by Dedicated customers? Check dedicated contract clauses before global rollback.
- Do we need a temporary rate-limit increase for core enterprise customers? CS to identify top-5 tenant IDs.

Actions after stabilization (post-mortem seed):
- Owner: Asha — coordinate post-mortem doc and add timeline export.
- ENG: run quick kernel-sensitivity test on eu-west traffic pattern (ticket ENG-5299).
- OPTIMIZE: add this case to batching config heuristics (PR candidate).
- SRE: revisit TL-EU-03 rule thresholds, add a suppression for short bursts <7s.
- CS: send update to impacted accounts with ETA and remediation steps.

Appendix (quick paste-ready commands / links):
- Monitoring alert query (paste into Grafana): grafana/query?q=rate_limiter_fire_count%20%7C%20region%3D%22eu-west-1%22
- Capacity snapshot location: gs://redwood-capacity/eu-west-1/snapshots/2028-02-12-1200.json
- Rollback PR (serving-runtime): github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1982

Notes to self (informal):
- If this doc is used during an incident, append a final "time-closed" row and snapshot the sheet as CSV to the incident ticket.
- Keep this file lean — move fuller post-mortem to Confluence and link back.

Mini retrospective (first-pass, to be refined):
- What worked: quick fallback routing, short-burst suppression prevented larger outage.
- What didn't: alert sensitivity and cross-team notification lag (~6m).
- Quick fix: 1) lower alert sensitivity on TL-EU-03 for tiny bursts, 2) add Slack auto-ping to "ops-hot" channel on rule fire, 3) pre-authorize limited temporary rate-bump for top-5 customers.

Last edited notes:
- Drafted by Asha; shared with SRE/ENG/CS on 2028-02-12 12:58 UTC.
- Intend to convert to a lightweight sheet (3 columns view) and pin to shared drive for week of Feb 12–18 for rapid reuse. 

End of doc.
